subject: Emberlytics — deployment & SLO playbook (post-call recap)

Subject: Emberlytics — deployment & SLO playbook (post-call recap)

Thanks for the time today — quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Really appreciate the context on your latency-sensitive scoring use case.

Key pain points we heard
- Production p99 latency spikes during morning batch window (~08:00-10:00 PT) that cause timeouts for downstream decisioning.
- Cost unpredictability when you scale model sizes for edge cases; need predictable unit economics for forecasting.
- Security requirement: PHI-filtered payloads; team prefers VPC/private deployment for audit logs.

Goals you stated
- p50/p95 target: 30ms / 120ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens).
- p99 target: <= 450ms for 90% of traffic; allow up to 800ms for long-context (>=2048 tokens) fallbacks.
- Sustained throughput: 220 qps with 2x burst to 500 qps during peak periods.

Model & data constraints
- Core model family: 13B-class dense/quantized variant (approx LLM-13B equivalence).
- Typical context: 512 tokens; occasional 4k contexts for long-session retrospection (~5% of requests).
- KV-cache reuse expected for sessionized interactions (avg reuse ratio ~6x).

Recommended topology (initial proposal)
- Private Redwood deployment in your AWS VPC (for audit/KMS) serving as primary inference lane.
- Dedicated GPU pool (A10G / H100 small-pod mix) sized for steady-state 220 qps with autoscaling to handle bursts to 500 qps.
- Streaming + continuous batching enabled; prefix/KV caching and routing policy to send long-context pieces to a quantized variant to keep p99 bounds tight.
- Fallback policy: if private capacity constrained, route to hosted Redwood-verified 13B quantized instance (with reduced token window) — will add an SLA note.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) We will send a draft mutual action plan (MPA) and a SLO matrix for you to validate (attached: emberlytics_slo_matrix.xlsx).
2) Can you share a representative traces sample (1 hour) and a small traffic histogram (token lengths + QPS by minute) so our infra team can run a cost/size simulation?
3) Planned follow-up: 30–45 min ops review with your infra + security leads; propose Tue 8/8 or Wed 8/9 (I listed a couple slots below).

Proposed meeting slots (PT)
- Tue 2028-08-08 09:00–09:45
- Tue 2028-08-08 13:00–13:45
- Wed 2028-08-09 10:00–10:45

Attachments: emberlytics_slo_matrix.xlsx (SLO targets + expected cost delta), redwood_proposal_v1.pdf (commercial sketch).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rishi and Karthik to start sizing.

On Thu, Aug 2, 2028 at 15:02 Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Key pain points we heard
> - Production p99 latency spikes during morning batch window (~08:00-10:00 PT) that cause timeouts for downstream decisioning.

Thanks for the recap — adding technical context and a short ops playbook sketch.

Notes from an infra sizing POV:
- Batching and latency: for 13B-class quantized models, we expect p50/p95 to be dominated by GPU compute; continuous batching at 20–40ms batching window will improve throughput with minimal p95 impact. We’ll model for a 30ms median batch delay to meet p50 target.
- Autoscaling: suggest a two-tier pool: small-pod low-latency nodes (1x A10G) for steady-state and larger pods (4x H100 or 8x A10G pooled) for burst handling. This hybrid reduces tail latency for short prompts.
- KV-cache: given 6x reuse, prefix caching should cut average compute by ~35% — we’ll include a caching sensitivity run in the sim.
- Long-contexts: route >=2048-token requests to a quantized long-window variant and increase token-aggregation windows to amortize token compute (keeps p99 below 800ms).

Security/compliance notes:
- For 1-year audit retention we recommend integrating customer KMS + S3 lifecycle policy; we’ll include retention config in the deployment manifest.

Actionables on our side before the ops review:
1) Run a cost/latency simulation against the traffic histogram (need the sample traces Aaron requested).
2) Draft a deployment manifest (private VPC, node types, autoscale policies) and share as a one-pager.
3) Provide SOC2 summary and log-retention options for procurement.

I’ll start the simulation once we have traces — Olga, feel free to push the sample to the secure upload link in the MPA doc (see related_links).
